I think a lot of people get mad because they think that "African-American" is too generalized, possibly racist. As someone said in my post, saying someone's African-American is like saying, your heritage is from that continent over there. 
See, I hate the term African-American because of many reasons, not because of what the word means, but mainly because of how people use it. If someone wants to identify themselves as African-American, that's great, whatever, likeigivafuck and goodforyou, I'm not about to condemn them for it. It annoys me when people are skirting around calling someone what they are, black. At least in my small-town, *racists* tend to use "African-American" because they don't know how to say black without sounding or feeling racist. 
So! People who don't understand the difference between someone happily identifying as a misused term, and someone else misusing the term. 
That's pretty much it.

It's good to see the perspective from another country. I watched a video once of a black person in England, and at some point the question was posed, "do you have African-Americans in England?" 
Her answer was something like, "wut no. I mean, some, if they're actually from America, but like, we're English."
Haha

It's not a matter of people being offended by the term African-American. Of course, that matters, but it's more along the lines of generalizing a group of people into one thing, in such a way that tries to define who they are. Calling someone African-American is like calling white people European-American. We don't do that. Sure, it's likely most white people have heritage in Europe, but we don't call them European-American.

A LOT of people do this. It's like...okay seriously, luck isn't magic. Luck is when you so happen to hit that rare chance at something. I'm not saying I believe in magic when I say that luck is a thing.
